questions.question_text: $O$ is the centre of a circle of radius $13$ cm. $BC$ is a chord of length $10$ cm, and $OM \perp BC$ at $M$. Find $OM$.

options.why: Finds $BM = 10 \div 2 = 5$ cm but gives the half-chord length as $OM$.
Uses the full chord length in Pythagoras' theorem, calculating $\sqrt{13^2-10^2}$ instead of using $BM = 5$ cm.

questions.solution_text:
$BM = 10 \div 2 = 5$ cm (the perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord)
$OB = 13$ cm (radius)
$OM = \sqrt{OB^2-BM^2} = \sqrt{13^2-5^2} = \sqrt{144} = 12$ cm

questions.question_text: $O$ is the centre of a circle. $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on the circle, with $C$ on the major arc $AB$. $\angle AOB = 82^{\circ}$. Find $\angle ACB$.

options.why: Copies the central angle instead of halving it.
Doubles the central angle instead of halving it to find the circumference angle.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ACB = \angle AOB \div 2$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)
$\angle ACB = 82^{\circ} \div 2 = 41^{\circ}$

options.why: Copies the given angle instead of using the angle sum of the right-angled triangle.
Gives $\angle ABC$, the semicircle angle, instead of the remaining angle $\angle BCA$.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ABC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$\angle BCA = 180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-28^{\circ} = 62^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABC$)

questions.question_text: $O$ is the centre of a circle. $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on the circle, with $B$ on the minor arc $AC$. The smaller angle $\angle AOC = 146^{\circ}$. Find $\angle ABC$.

options.why: Halves the smaller central angle instead of the reflex central angle standing on the same arc as $\angle ABC$.
Finds the reflex central angle $360^{\circ}-146^{\circ}$ but forgets to halve it.

questions.solution_text:
Reflex $\angle AOC = 360^{\circ}-146^{\circ} = 214^{\circ}$ (angles in a revolution)
$\angle ABC = 214^{\circ} \div 2 = 107^{\circ}$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)

questions.question_text: $BD$ is a diameter of a circle of radius $6.5$ cm. $C$ lies on the circle and $BC = 5$ cm. Find $DC$.

options.why: Subtracts the given side from the diameter, calculating $13-5$, instead of using Pythagoras' theorem.
Adds the diameter and the given side, calculating $13+5$, instead of using Pythagoras' theorem.

questions.solution_text:
$BD = 2 \times 6.5 = 13$ cm
$\angle BCD = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$DC = \sqrt{BD^2-BC^2} = \sqrt{13^2-5^2} = \sqrt{144} = 12$ cm

questions.question_text:
$A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie on a circle with centre $O$ in that order. Side $CD$ is extended beyond $D$ to $E$.
The exterior angle $\angle ADE = 64^{\circ}$.
Find the smaller central angle $\angle AOC$.

options.why: Finds the opposite interior angle $\angle ABC = 64^{\circ}$ but forgets to double it to find the central angle.
Halves $64^{\circ}$ instead of doubling the matching circumference angle to find the central angle.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ABC = \angle ADE = 64^{\circ}$ (an exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the opposite interior angle)
$\angle AOC = 2 \times \angle ABC$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)
$\angle AOC = 2 \times 64^{\circ} = 128^{\circ}$

questions.question_text: $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie on a circle in that order. $\angle ABD = 29^{\circ}$. Find $\angle ACD$.

options.why: Doubles the given circumference angle, giving the matching central angle instead of the other circumference angle.
Subtracts $29^{\circ}$ from $180^{\circ}$ as though the requested angles were opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ACD = \angle ABD$ (angles at the circumference standing on the same arc $AD$ are equal)
$\angle ACD = 29^{\circ}$

options.why: Finds $OM = 8$ cm correctly but doubles $OM$ instead of the half-chord length $BM$.
Finds $BM$ correctly but forgets that $M$ is the midpoint of $BD$, so $BD$ is double this.

questions.solution_text:
$O$ lies on $AC$, so $OM \perp BD$ too, and $M$ is the midpoint of $BD$ (perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord).
$OM = 10 - 2 = 8$ cm
$BM = \sqrt{OB^2-OM^2} = \sqrt{10^2-8^2} = \sqrt{36} = 6$ cm
$BD = 2 \times 6 = 12$ cm
